slides.heading: Largest Rectangle Under Skyline
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Hard · Stacks
slides.narration: Let's solve Largest Rectangle Under Skyline, a hard stacks problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Largest rectangle area within adjacent buildings of width 1.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Largest rectangle area within adjacent buildings of width 1. Monotonic increasing stack of indices.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: A monotonic stack finds, for each building, how far it extends left and right before a shorter one.
slides.narration: A monotonic stack finds, for each building, how far it extends left and right before a shorter one.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: For each bar expand left/right → O(n²)
slides.narration: Checking every range is quadratic. A monotonic increasing stack finds, for each bar, how far it can extend in both directions, and each bar is pushed and popped once.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. When a shorter building arrives, pop and compute area
3. Width spans to the new top
slides.narration: Step by step. First, push indices with increasing heights. Second, when a shorter building arrives, pop and compute area. Third, width spans to the new top. Fourth, flush at the end.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Pop 3: area 3
slides.narration: A lower bar arrives, so pop height 3. It extends from index 1 to 1, width 1, area 3, the best so far.

slides.caption: Pop 3: area 6
slides.narration: A lower bar arrives, so pop height 3. It extends from index 1 to 2, width 2, area 6, the best so far.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Pop 2: area 8
slides.narration: A lower bar arrives, so pop height 2. It extends from index 1 to 4, width 4, area 8, the best so far.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Pop 1: area 9
slides.narration: A lower bar arrives, so pop height 1. It extends from index 0 to 8, width 9, area 9, the best so far.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: For i up to n, with height zero at the end, pop while the top is at least the current height, computing height times i minus new top minus one. Push i.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is O of n.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Sentinel 0 at the end flushes the stack
Width uses the new top as left boundary
slides.narration: A zero sentinel at the end flushes remaining bars.

slides.narration: Apply it row by row for the maximal rectangle in a binary matrix.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: A monotonic stack finds, for each building, how far it extends left and right before a shorter one.
slides.narration: To recap Largest Rectangle Under Skyline: A monotonic stack finds, for each building, how far it extends left and right before a shorter one. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
